checklist.step: Confirm the required oversight-function roles are filled and mapped to the org chart
actions: Pull the current organization chart from the HRIS (Workday/SuccessFactors) and confirm named incumbents exist for Chief Risk Officer, Chief Audit Executive and Chief Compliance Officer (Head of Compliance).

Cross-check each incumbent's reporting line: CRO and CAE must report functionally to the Board (or Board Risk/Audit Committee) with a dotted or solid administrative line to the CEO, not into a business line.
Flag any oversight-function role that is vacant, filled on an interim basis, or reporting into a business-line executive.
Escalate any gap found to the Chief Risk Officer and General Counsel the same week.
checklist.done: every oversight-function role is filled, mapped, and its reporting line is confirmed independent of the business lines it oversees

checklist.step: Review and refresh committee charters against the Corporate Governance Guideline content standard
actions: Open the Board Risk Committee, Audit Committee and Conduct Review Committee charters in the board portal's document library.
Check each charter states the committee's authority to access records, staff and external advisors without management gatekeeping.
Check each charter names the resources (budget, headcount) the committee can commission for independent advice.
Redline any charter missing the unfettered-access or resourcing clause and route it to General Counsel for legal review.
Version and date-stamp the refreshed charter in the board portal.
checklist.done: each committee charter carries current unfettered-access and resourcing language, version-stamped in the board portal

checklist.step: Confirm CRO/CAE/CCO appointment and removal require Board Risk Committee or Board approval
actions: Check the delegation-of-authority matrix in the GRC platform confirms CRO, CAE and CCO appointments and removals are a Board (not CEO-delegated) decision.
Confirm the most recent CRO/CAE/CCO appointment or reappointment has a Board or committee resolution on file.
Where a delegation gap exists, draft a Board resolution correcting it and calendar it for the next Board meeting.
checklist.done: the delegation-of-authority matrix and Board minutes together evidence Board-level control over oversight-function appointments and removals

checklist.step: Maintain the committee membership roster and meeting calendar
actions: In the board portal, open Governance ▸ Committees and update each committee's member list, independence designation and term dates.
Confirm the Board Risk Committee and Audit Committee each meet the minimum independent-member composition set in the charter.
Publish the annual meeting calendar with at least four Board Risk Committee sittings and confirm dates against the ORSA and capital-planning cycle.
checklist.done: the board portal roster reflects current, independence-compliant membership and a published meeting calendar exists for the year

checklist.step: Prepare and distribute Board Risk Committee meeting materials
actions: Compile the risk dashboard, top-risk register extract and any OSFI supervisory correspondence into the committee pack.
Upload the pack to the board portal at least 5 business days ahead of the meeting per the charter's notice period.
Confirm the Chief Audit Executive and Head of Compliance have added their oversight-function status updates to the pack.
checklist.done: the committee pack is complete and posted to the board portal within the charter's notice period

checklist.step: Hold a private session between the CRO/CAE/CCO and the committee without management present
actions: Schedule a standing private-session agenda item at least annually on the Board Risk Committee, Audit Committee and Conduct Review Committee calendars.
Confirm the CEO and other executive management leave the room (or call) for the private-session minutes segment.
Have the Corporate Secretary record that the private session occurred, without capturing content that would compromise its purpose, in the minutes.
checklist.done: minutes show a private session occurred with each oversight-function head at least once in the year

checklist.step: Record Board and committee minutes evidencing oversight-function access and decisions
actions: Draft minutes capturing attendance, decisions taken, dissent recorded, and any items the CRO/CAE/CCO raised directly with the committee.
Circulate draft minutes to committee members for correction within 10 business days of the meeting.
File the approved minutes in the board portal's permanent minute book, indexed by committee and meeting date.
checklist.done: approved, indexed minutes exist in the board portal for every Board and committee meeting held in the period

checklist.step: Review oversight-function resourcing (budget and headcount) annually
actions: Compare current-year Risk, Compliance and Internal Audit headcount and budget to the prior year and to the entity's risk profile growth.
Document the resourcing adequacy conclusion and any request for additional headcount in the annual resourcing memo.
Route the memo to the Board Risk Committee for review alongside the annual charter refresh.
checklist.done: a dated resourcing-adequacy memo for each oversight function is on file and reviewed by the Board Risk Committee

checklist.step: Track and notify OSFI of responsible-persons changes as required under the ICA
actions: On any change to a director, CEO, CRO, Chief Actuary, Appointed Actuary or (for a foreign branch) Chief Agent, open a responsible-persons change file.
Confirm the incoming individual's fitness-and-propriety file is complete before the appointment is effective.
Prepare and submit the OSFI notification per the ICA responsible-persons provisions, including biographical affidavit where required.
File the submission confirmation in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: every responsible-persons change has a completed fitness file and a filed OSFI notification with confirmation on record

checklist.step: Update the governance manual and org charts for structural changes
actions: On any committee restructuring, role redefinition or reporting-line change, update the governance manual stored in SharePoint's Governance library.
Republish the updated org chart and circulate the change summary to the Board Governance Lead and General Counsel.
Version the manual and retain prior versions for audit trail.
checklist.done: the governance manual and org chart in SharePoint reflect the current structure with a versioned change history

checklist.step: Reconcile the GRC platform's governance module to the board portal's charter and roster records
actions: Open the GRC platform's governance/entity-structure module and compare committee names, mandates and membership counts to the board portal.
Correct any mismatch and note the correction date.
Confirm the GRC platform's control owner field for each governance control points to the correct oversight-function head.
checklist.done: the GRC platform and board portal show identical committee structure and membership with no unresolved mismatch

checklist.step: Conduct the annual committee effectiveness self-assessment
actions: Distribute the committee effectiveness questionnaire to all Board and committee members covering mandate clarity, access, resourcing and meeting cadence.
Compile responses and identify any recurring gap, such as insufficient notice period or a resourcing shortfall.
Present the self-assessment summary and remediation actions to the full Board.
checklist.done: a compiled self-assessment with remediation actions is presented to the Board within the fiscal year

checklist.step: File the annual charter and structure package in the compliance evidence repository
actions: Assemble the refreshed charters, org chart, resourcing memos, delegation-of-authority matrix and self-assessment into a single annual governance package.
Upload the package to the compliance evidence repository under the fiscal year and tag it 'OSFI Corporate Governance Guideline'.
Confirm the package is retrievable by committee name and fiscal year in the repository index.
checklist.done: the annual governance package is filed, tagged and retrievable in the compliance evidence repository

checklist.step: Brief the Board on any OSFI Corporate Governance Guideline update and assess impact
actions: Monitor OSFI publications and industry counsel updates for revisions to the Corporate Governance Guideline or related guidelines (A-4, E-13).
Prepare a gap analysis comparing the current governance structure to any new requirement.
Present the gap analysis and remediation plan to the Board Governance Lead and Board Risk Committee.
checklist.done: a gap analysis exists for every Corporate Governance Guideline revision issued in the period, with a remediation plan if gaps are found

checklist.step: Escalate and close unresolved governance-structure gaps before the next OSFI supervisory review
actions: Compile all open items from the self-assessment, GRC reconciliation and OSFI guideline gap analysis into a single remediation tracker.
Assign an owner and target date to each open item in the GRC platform.
Confirm closure evidence is attached before marking an item closed, and report residual open items to the Board Risk Committee ahead of any scheduled OSFI supervisory meeting.
checklist.done: the remediation tracker shows every governance-structure gap closed or has a Board-visible open item with owner and date ahead of the next OSFI supervisory review

testing.step: Build the population of oversight-function roles and governance committees in scope
actions: Extract from the GRC platform's governance module every oversight-function role (CRO, CAE, CCO) and every Board committee active in the period.
Reconcile the extract to the HRIS org chart and the board portal roster.
Resolve any count mismatch before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled across the GRC platform, HRIS and board portal and signed as complete

testing.step: Sample charters and reporting lines for independent re-review
actions: Select all Board Risk, Audit and Conduct Review Committee charters plus a random sample of two other governance committees.
For each, independently assess whether the charter grants unfettered access and adequate resourcing, without reading the prior sign-off first.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded self-assessment result and flag any disagreement as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled charter has an independent re-assessment note and any disagreement is flagged

testing.step: Re-perform the reporting-line independence check
actions: For each oversight-function head in the sample, trace the reporting line in the HRIS org chart from the individual up to the Board or committee.
Confirm no business-line executive sits between the oversight-function head and the Board on matters of independence and access.
Flag any indirect or dotted-line structure that could compromise independence.
testing.done: reporting-line independence is independently confirmed or exceptioned for every sampled role

testing.step: Verify Board and committee minutes evidence the required private sessions
actions: Open the board portal minute book for the Board Risk, Audit and Conduct Review Committees for the period.
Confirm each committee's minutes record at least one private session with the relevant oversight-function head, management excluded.
Note any committee missing a private session in the period as an exception.
testing.done: private-session evidence is confirmed in the minutes for every in-scope committee or an exception is logged

testing.step: Confirm appointment/removal decisions for CRO, CAE and CCO were made at Board level
actions: Pull any CRO, CAE or CCO appointment, reappointment or removal that occurred in the test period.
Trace each to a Board or Board Risk Committee resolution in the minute book.
Flag any appointment or removal actioned without a traceable Board-level resolution.
testing.done: every in-period appointment or removal traces to a Board-level resolution, or is logged as an exception

testing.step: Trace responsible-persons OSFI notifications to filed confirmations
actions: For each responsible-persons change in the test period, pull the fitness file and the OSFI notification from the compliance evidence repository.
Confirm the notification was submitted within the timeframe the ICA responsible-persons provisions require and a submission confirmation is on file.
Flag any change notified late or without confirmation on file.
testing.done: every sampled responsible-persons change has a timely, confirmed OSFI notification, or an exception is logged

testing.step: Recompute oversight-function resourcing adequacy against the risk-profile trend
actions: Pull three years of Risk, Compliance and Internal Audit headcount and budget from the HRIS and Finance records.
Compare the trend to the entity's asset growth, new-business growth and risk-profile changes over the same period.
Note any resourcing flat-line or decline against a materially growing risk profile as a finding for the Board Risk Committee.
testing.done: a resourcing trend analysis is completed and any adverse trend is documented as a finding

testing.step: Verify the GRC platform and board portal remain reconciled at test date
actions: Compare the GRC platform's governance module to the board portal roster and charter set as of the test date.
Identify any structural or membership discrepancy not yet corrected.
Log each open discrepancy as an exception with the date first identified.
testing.done: the two systems are confirmed reconciled at test date, or every discrepancy is logged as an aged exception

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker entry for each testing exception (missing private session, late notification, unreconciled charter, resourcing gap).
Assign a root cause category (process gap, staffing gap, system gap) and an owner from Corporate Secretary, General Counsel or the relevant oversight-function head.
Set a remediation date and carry unresolved items into the next annual test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an owner, root cause and remediation date, and open items carry forward to the next test cycle

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the governance-structure test
actions: Compute the exception count against the zero-tolerance standard for Board-level appointment/removal and private-session evidence.
Write the test conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the underlying evidence.
Have an independent reviewer who did not author the sampled assessments sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any open exceptions to the Board Risk Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the Board Risk Committee

checklist.step: Confirm the annual filing calendar for CGAD, holding-company forms and the climate disclosure
actions: Open the Internal Regulatory System filing calendar and confirm entries exist for the CGAD, any holding-company return and the B-15 climate disclosure, each with a due date derived from fiscal year-end.
Cross-check the climate disclosure due date is set to fiscal year-end plus 180 days, not a calendar-year assumption.
Assign a preparer and a reviewer to each filing line in the calendar.
checklist.done: the filing calendar carries a due date, preparer and reviewer for the CGAD, holding-company forms and the climate disclosure

checklist.step: Collect governance data for the CGAD / holding-company forms
actions: Request from the Board Governance Lead the current committee structure, director biographies and independence assessments.
Request from General Counsel any material governance events in the fiscal year, such as leadership changes, structural changes or material litigation affecting governance.
Populate the CGAD data template with the collected information, citing the source document for each field.
checklist.done: the CGAD data template is fully populated with sourced governance data

checklist.step: Collect climate-related governance and strategy content for the B-15 disclosure
actions: Request from the Board Risk Committee minutes evidence of climate-risk oversight, including frequency of review and decisions taken.
Request from the Chief Risk Officer the climate-risk integration into the enterprise risk framework and risk appetite statement.
Document the entity's climate strategy, including transition plan status and material climate-related opportunities considered.
checklist.done: governance and strategy content for the climate disclosure is drafted with named sources for each statement

checklist.step: Compile climate risk management process content
actions: Document the process for identifying, assessing and managing physical and transition climate risks, referencing the risk register entries tagged 'Climate'.
Confirm the description matches how climate risk is actually integrated into the ORSA process, not an aspirational description.
Have the Chief Risk Officer review the risk-management section for accuracy against the current ORSA report.
checklist.done: the risk-management section is reviewed by the Chief Risk Officer and matches the current ORSA content

checklist.step: Compile climate metrics and targets
actions: Pull Scope 1/2 (and Scope 3 where in scope) emissions data and any climate-related financial exposure metrics from the data pipeline orchestrator (Airflow/Dagster/Prefect) output used for ESG reporting.
Confirm the metrics methodology note (boundary, estimation approach, restatements) is included.
State any climate-related targets, the baseline year and progress to date, or explicitly state none exist.
checklist.done: metrics and targets are stated with methodology and progress, or their absence is explicitly disclosed

checklist.step: Draft the disclosure document aligned to B-15 Chapter 2 structure
actions: Assemble the governance, strategy, risk management and metrics/targets sections into the disclosure document using the B-15-aligned template.
Cross-reference each disclosure statement to its supporting source document in a working paper.
Circulate the draft to the Chief Financial Officer and Chief Risk Officer for content review.
checklist.done: a complete draft with source cross-references exists and has been circulated for content review

checklist.step: Obtain legal and financial review of the draft disclosure
actions: Review the draft for consistency with financial statement disclosures and forward-looking-statement language requirements.
Confirm no statement creates an unsupported forward commitment or contradicts the Annual Information Form or MD&A.
Return the draft with tracked-change comments to Sustainability Risk Manager.
checklist.done: legal review is complete with tracked comments resolved before Board submission

checklist.step: Route the disclosure and CGAD/holding-company forms for Board approval
actions: Upload the final draft disclosure and CGAD data package to the board portal ahead of the scheduled Board or Board Risk Committee meeting.
Present the package for approval, noting any legal review comments and their resolution.
Record the approval, any conditions, and the approving body in the minutes.
checklist.done: Board or committee approval of the disclosure and CGAD package is recorded in the minutes

checklist.step: Publish the climate disclosure publicly within the 180-day window
actions: Confirm with the Chief Financial Officer the exact fiscal year-end date and compute the 180-day publication deadline.
Publish the approved disclosure on the corporate website's investor relations or regulatory disclosures page.
Record the publication date and URL in the filing calendar entry.
checklist.done: the disclosure is published at the URL on record on or before fiscal year-end plus 180 days

checklist.step: Submit the CGAD and any holding-company return to OSFI
actions: Log in to OSFI's Regulatory Reporting System (RRS) and open the CGAD / holding-company return submission for the reporting entity.
Upload the approved data package and complete all required return fields and attestations.
Submit and download the system-generated submission confirmation and reference number.
checklist.done: the CGAD/holding-company return is submitted in OSFI's RRS with a confirmation and reference number on file

checklist.step: File submission and publication confirmations in the compliance evidence repository
actions: Upload the OSFI RRS confirmation, the published disclosure PDF, the publication URL screenshot, and the Board approval minute extract into a single filing package.
Tag the package with the fiscal year and 'B-15 climate disclosure' / 'CGAD'.
Confirm the package is retrievable in the repository index by fiscal year.
checklist.done: a complete, tagged evidence package is filed and retrievable by fiscal year

checklist.step: Track and close any correction needed to a published disclosure
actions: If an error is identified post-publication, assess materiality with the Chief Financial Officer.
Where material, draft a correction notice, obtain Board approval, and republish with a change log.
File the correction and its approval in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: any material post-publication correction is Board-approved, republished with a change log, and filed

checklist.step: Reconcile the disclosure filing calendar to actual completion dates
actions: At fiscal year-close, mark each calendar line (CGAD, holding-company form, climate disclosure) with its actual submission or publication date.
Flag any line completed after its due date.
Feed any late-filing pattern into next year's calendar planning to build in more lead time.
checklist.done: the filing calendar shows actual completion dates for every line and any lateness is flagged

checklist.step: Brief the Board on upcoming B-15 or CGAD requirement changes
actions: Monitor OSFI publications for updates to Guideline B-15 or CGAD/holding-company return requirements.
Summarize any change and its impact on next year's disclosure scope or template.
Present the summary to the Board Risk Committee ahead of the next filing cycle.
checklist.done: a change-impact summary is presented ahead of any OSFI B-15 or CGAD requirement update taking effect

checklist.step: Escalate any missed deadline immediately to General Counsel and the CFO
actions: On detecting the 180-day climate disclosure deadline or an OSFI return due date will be missed, notify General Counsel and the Chief Financial Officer the same business day.
Prepare a late-filing notice or self-identification memo for submission to OSFI where the deadline has already passed.
Log the missed deadline as a compliance exception with root cause and a corrective-action date.
checklist.done: any missed deadline triggers same-day escalation and a logged exception with corrective action

testing.step: Build the population of governance and climate disclosures due in the test period
actions: Extract the filing calendar for every CGAD, holding-company form and climate disclosure due in the fiscal year under test.
Reconcile the extract to the entity list of OSFI-regulated subsidiaries/branches to confirm nothing is missing.
Resolve any count discrepancy before sampling.
testing.done: the disclosure population is reconciled to the entity list and signed complete

testing.step: Confirm each disclosure was filed or published on or before its due date
actions: For every population item, compare the recorded submission/publication date to the computed due date (fiscal year-end plus 180 days for climate; OSFI calendar date for CGAD).
List any item filed or published after its due date as an exception.
testing.done: every population item's timeliness is confirmed or logged as an exception

testing.step: Trace the climate disclosure content to its supporting source documents
actions: Select the current-year climate disclosure and pull the working paper cross-references for governance, strategy, risk management and metrics sections.
Independently verify each cross-referenced statement against the source (Board minutes, ORSA report, emissions data extract).
Flag any statement that cannot be traced to a source or is inconsistent with it.
testing.done: every sampled disclosure statement is traced to a verifiable source, or logged as an exception

testing.step: Recompute the 180-day publication deadline
actions: Independently compute fiscal year-end plus 180 days for the entity.
Compare to the deadline recorded in the filing calendar and to the actual publication date.
Flag any discrepancy in the deadline computation or a publication after the recomputed date.
testing.done: the 180-day deadline is independently recomputed and confirmed against the actual publication date

testing.step: Verify OSFI RRS submission confirmations for the CGAD / holding-company return
actions: Pull the OSFI RRS submission confirmation and reference number for the sampled return from the compliance evidence repository.
Confirm the confirmation date, entity name and return type match the population record.
Flag any return with no confirmation on file.
testing.done: every sampled return has a matching, verified OSFI RRS confirmation on file

testing.step: Confirm Board approval preceded publication/submission
actions: Open the board portal minute book and locate the approval minute for the sampled disclosure or return.
Confirm the approval date is earlier than the publication or submission date.
Flag any disclosure published or submitted before Board approval was recorded.
testing.done: Board approval is confirmed to pre-date publication/submission for every sampled item

testing.step: Verify the emissions and climate metrics methodology
actions: Pull the underlying emissions data extract and methodology note referenced in the climate disclosure.
Recompute a sample metric, such as total Scope 1+2 emissions, from the source extract and compare to the published figure.
Flag any variance beyond a rounding tolerance.
testing.done: the sampled metric recomputation matches the published figure within tolerance, or is logged as an exception

testing.step: Confirm any post-publication correction was Board-approved and disclosed
actions: Identify any correction made to a disclosure in the test period from the compliance evidence repository.
Confirm a Board approval and a change log accompany the correction.
Flag any correction made without documented Board approval.
testing.done: every correction in the period has documented Board approval and a change log, or is logged as an exception

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker entry for each testing exception (late filing, untraceable statement, metric variance, missing approval).
Assign a root cause and an owner from Corporate Secretary, Sustainability Risk Manager or Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Set a remediation date and carry unresolved items into the next annual test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an owner, root cause and remediation date

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the disclosure test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance standard for missed statutory deadlines.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence.
Have an independent reviewer who did not prepare the disclosure sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the Board Risk Committee

Request the candidate complete the fitness-and-propriety questionnaire covering integrity, competence and financial soundness.
checklist.done: a candidate record exists in the HRIS with the questionnaire request logged

checklist.step: Collect and verify integrity information

checklist.done: criminal record, disciplinary and bankruptcy checks are completed and any disclosed item is cross-checked

checklist.step: Collect and verify competence information
actions: Request the candidate's CV, professional designations and reference contacts relevant to the proposed role.
Contact at least two professional references and record the substance of each conversation.
Confirm any required professional designation (e.g., FCIA for Appointed Actuary, FCPA for CFO) is current and in good standing with the issuing body.
checklist.done: competence evidence is collected, references documented and any required designation confirmed current

checklist.step: Collect and verify financial-soundness information
actions: Request a credit check consistent with the entity's assessment procedure and the candidate's consent.
Review the credit check for material adverse findings such as bankruptcy, judgment or significant delinquency.
Document the financial-soundness conclusion on the assessment record.
checklist.done: a credit check is completed and reviewed, with a documented financial-soundness conclusion

checklist.step: Assemble the assessment summary and route for legal review
actions: Compile the integrity, competence and financial-soundness findings into a single assessment summary.
Assess whether any finding meets the entity's adverse-finding threshold requiring escalation.
Confirm the summary cites the source of each finding (check provider, reference name, designation registry).
checklist.done: a sourced assessment summary exists with an explicit adverse-finding determination

checklist.step: Escalate any adverse finding before the appointment proceeds
actions: Where an adverse finding exists, brief the Board Governance Lead and, for director nominations, the Board Nominating/Governance Committee before any vote.
Document the mitigating factors considered and the final go/no-go decision with its rationale.
Where the decision proceeds despite an adverse finding, obtain written Board sign-off on the rationale.
checklist.done: any adverse finding is escalated and documented with a Board-level decision and rationale before appointment

checklist.step: Obtain Board or committee approval of the appointment
actions: Present the candidate's assessment summary, without unnecessary personal detail, to the Board or the relevant committee for approval.
Record the approval vote and date in the minutes.
Confirm the effective date of appointment is set on or after the approval date.
checklist.done: the appointment approval and date are recorded in the minutes and the effective date follows approval

checklist.step: File the biographical affidavit and OSFI notification where required
actions: Prepare the biographical affidavit or equivalent OSFI-required form for the responsible-persons category.
Submit the notification per the ICA responsible-persons provisions ahead of or concurrent with the appointment taking effect.
File the submission confirmation with the assessment record.
checklist.done: the biographical affidavit is filed and the OSFI notification submitted with confirmation on record

checklist.step: Close and file the completed assessment record
actions: Upload the completed questionnaire, checks, reference notes, assessment summary and Board approval into the compliance evidence repository.
Tag the record with the individual's name, role and appointment date.
Set the next reconfirmation due date, 3 years from appointment, in the HRIS.
checklist.done: the completed assessment file is retained and a reconfirmation due date is set

checklist.step: Run the periodic reconfirmation on the 3-year cycle
actions: On the HRIS reconfirmation alert, reopen the individual's file and request an updated integrity, competence and financial-soundness disclosure.
Re-run the criminal record and credit checks and re-verify any professional designation is still current.
Compare results to the prior assessment and flag any new adverse item.
checklist.done: the reconfirmation checks are complete and any new adverse item is flagged

checklist.step: Monitor for adverse-information triggers between reconfirmation cycles
actions: Maintain a watch on public disciplinary registers and news alerts for named responsible persons between scheduled reconfirmations.
On receiving an adverse-information trigger, open an out-of-cycle assessment the same week.
Route the out-of-cycle finding through the same escalation path as a new appointment.
checklist.done: an out-of-cycle assessment is opened within a week of any adverse-information trigger

checklist.step: Notify OSFI of any responsible-persons departure or removal
actions: On any resignation, removal or non-renewal of a responsible person, prepare the departure notification per the ICA provisions.
State the effective date and, where applicable, the reason for removal.
Submit and file the confirmation in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: every departure or removal is notified to OSFI with a filed confirmation

checklist.step: Maintain the responsible-persons register
actions: Keep a current register of every individual holding a responsible-persons role, their appointment date, last reconfirmation date and next due date.
Reconcile the register to the HRIS and the compliance evidence repository quarterly.
Circulate the register to General Counsel and the Board Governance Lead each quarter.
checklist.done: a reconciled responsible-persons register is circulated quarterly

checklist.step: Train HR Business Partners and General Counsel staff on the assessment procedure
actions: Deliver an annual refresher on the fitness-and-propriety procedure, including how to recognize an adverse-finding threshold.
Update the procedure for any change in OSFI expectations or check-provider process.
Record attendance and the procedure version acknowledged.
checklist.done: annual training is delivered and attendance recorded against the current procedure version

checklist.step: Escalate any lapsed reconfirmation to General Counsel immediately
actions: Where a reconfirmation is not completed by its due date, notify General Counsel the same week.
Open a compliance exception noting the lapse and the plan to complete the reconfirmation.
Do not allow the individual to continue in the responsible-persons role past a defined grace period without General Counsel sign-off.
checklist.done: every lapsed reconfirmation is escalated within a week and has a logged exception with a completion plan

testing.step: Build the population of responsible persons and their assessment due dates
actions: Extract from the HRIS every individual coded as a responsible-persons role, their appointment date and reconfirmation due date.
Reconcile the extract to the responsible-persons register maintained by the Corporate Secretary.
Resolve any mismatch before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the responsible-persons register and signed complete

testing.step: Select the sample of assessment files for re-review
actions: Take all individuals appointed or reconfirmed in the test period, plus a random sample of five active files not due for reconfirmation.
Record the population size, sample size and selection method in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn and its method is documented and reproducible

testing.step: Re-perform the integrity check re-review
actions: Pull the criminal record, disciplinary and bankruptcy check results for each sampled file.
Independently search public regulator disciplinary registers for the individual's name and compare to what is on file.
Flag any finding on file that is stale, incomplete, or contradicted by the independent search.
testing.done: each sampled integrity check is independently corroborated or logged as an exception

testing.step: Verify competence evidence and designation currency
actions: For each sampled file, confirm the required professional designation is listed as current on the issuing body's public registry as of the assessment date.
Confirm at least two reference contacts are documented with substantive notes, not a blank template.
testing.done: designation currency and reference documentation are independently confirmed for every sampled file

testing.step: Recompute the financial-soundness conclusion
actions: Pull the credit check result for each sampled file and independently assess it against the entity's adverse-finding threshold.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded financial-soundness conclusion and flag any disagreement.
testing.done: financial-soundness conclusions are independently re-derived and compared, with disagreements flagged

testing.step: Confirm Board approval pre-dates the appointment effective date
actions: Pull the Board or committee minute recording approval for each sampled appointment.
Compare the approval date to the appointment effective date recorded in the HRIS.
Flag any appointment effective before Board approval was recorded.
testing.done: Board approval is confirmed to pre-date the effective date for every sampled appointment

testing.step: Trace OSFI responsible-persons notifications to filed confirmations
actions: For each sampled appointment or departure, pull the OSFI notification submission confirmation from the compliance evidence repository.
Confirm the notification timing meets the ICA responsible-persons provisions.
Flag any missing or late notification.
testing.done: every sampled notification is confirmed filed and timely, or logged as an exception

testing.step: Verify reconfirmation cycles were completed on schedule
actions: For each sampled active file, compare the last reconfirmation date to the 3-year cycle requirement.
Flag any file past its reconfirmation due date without a documented out-of-cycle assessment or escalation.
testing.done: reconfirmation timeliness is confirmed for every sampled file, or exceptions are logged

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker entry for each testing exception (uncorroborated check, missing approval, late notification, lapsed reconfirmation).
Assign a root cause and an owner from HR Business Partner, General Counsel or Corporate Secretary.
Set a remediation date and carry unresolved items into the next test cycle.
testing.done: every exception has an owner, root cause and remediation date

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the fitness-and-propriety test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance standard for missing pre-appointment assessments.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence.
Have an independent reviewer who did not perform the sampled assessments sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Board Governance Lead and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the Board Governance Lead

checklist.step: Compile the governance policy inventory and last-review dates
actions: Open the board portal's policy library and list every governance policy, including the risk appetite statement, business/strategic plan, internal control framework, reinsurance risk policy and climate governance policy, with its last Board approval date.
Flag any policy not reviewed in the prior 12 months for priority review.
Confirm ownership is assigned for each policy, naming which executive drafts revisions.
checklist.done: a current inventory exists with last-review dates and an assigned owner per policy

checklist.step: Gather management's proposed updates to the business/strategic plan
actions: Compile the proposed business strategy update, including market assumptions, growth targets and capital implications.
Request the Chief Financial Officer confirm the plan's capital and solvency implications are consistent with the current Internal Capital Target under Guideline A-4.
Request the Chief Risk Officer confirm the plan sits within the current risk appetite statement.
checklist.done: the proposed plan is drafted with confirmed capital and risk-appetite consistency from CFO and CRO

checklist.step: Review and propose updates to the risk appetite statement
actions: Compare the current risk appetite statement's qualitative statements and quantitative limits to the entity's actual risk profile and the proposed business plan.
Draft proposed limit or statement changes with rationale, referencing the ORSA report's risk-profile findings.
Confirm proposed changes remain consistent with the Board-approved capital targets.
checklist.done: risk appetite statement proposed changes are drafted with rationale tied to the ORSA report

checklist.step: Review the internal-control framework and controls-assurance summary
actions: Summarize the year's internal-control testing results, including any material control deficiency identified.
Recommend framework updates addressing any recurring deficiency theme.
Route the summary to the Board Governance Lead for inclusion in the annual policy package.
checklist.done: an internal-control summary with recommended updates is included in the annual policy package

checklist.step: Draft revisions to the reinsurance risk policy per Guideline B-3
actions: Review the current reinsurance risk policy against the entity's actual ceded-reinsurance concentration and counterparty credit exposure.
Propose updated counterparty limits or diversification requirements where concentration has changed materially.
Route the proposed policy to the Chief Risk Officer for risk-appetite consistency review.
checklist.done: reinsurance risk policy revisions are proposed and reviewed for risk-appetite consistency

checklist.step: Draft revisions to the climate governance policy per Guideline B-15 Chapter 1
actions: Review the climate governance policy against the current climate-risk assessment and any new OSFI B-15 guidance.
Propose updates to climate-risk oversight roles, escalation thresholds or scenario-analysis cadence.
Route the proposed policy to the Chief Risk Officer for consolidation with the risk appetite statement.
checklist.done: climate governance policy revisions are proposed and consolidated with the risk appetite review

checklist.step: Route all draft policies for legal review
actions: Upload each draft policy to iManage and review for consistency with statutory obligations and other Board-approved documents.
Confirm defined terms and approval-authority language are consistent across the policy suite.
Return redlined drafts to each policy owner with comments resolved before Board submission.
checklist.done: every draft policy has completed legal review in iManage with comments resolved

checklist.step: Assemble the annual governance policy package for the Board
actions: Compile the business/strategic plan, risk appetite statement, internal-control summary, reinsurance and climate governance policy revisions into a single Board package.
Upload the package to the board portal at least the charter-required notice period ahead of the meeting.
Include a cover memo summarizing each proposed change and its rationale.
checklist.done: a complete package with a change-summary memo is posted to the board portal within the notice period

checklist.step: Present the package and obtain Board approval
actions: Present the business plan, risk appetite statement and policy revisions to the Board, addressing questions on capital, risk-appetite and control implications.
Record the Board's approval, any amendments made in session, and any dissent, in the minutes.
Confirm the approved version is the one filed, not a pre-amendment draft.
checklist.done: Board approval, any in-session amendments and the final approved version are recorded in the minutes

checklist.step: Publish the approved policies to the organization
actions: Upload the final approved policies to the SharePoint governance library, superseding prior versions.
Notify policy owners and affected department heads of the changes and effective dates.
Update the policy inventory with the new approval date and version number.
checklist.done: approved policies are published in SharePoint with prior versions superseded and owners notified

checklist.step: Obtain management attestation that actions are consistent with the approved plan and risk appetite
actions: Issue a quarterly attestation request to each business-line executive confirming their actions remain within the approved risk appetite limits.
Compile attestation responses and flag any self-reported breach or near-breach.
Report the attestation summary to the Board Risk Committee.
checklist.done: quarterly attestations are collected and any breach or near-breach is reported to the Board Risk Committee

checklist.step: Monitor for interim triggers requiring an out-of-cycle policy review
actions: Define trigger events, such as a material acquisition, regulatory guideline change, or risk-appetite breach, requiring an interim review.
On a trigger event, initiate an out-of-cycle review of the affected policy within 30 days.
Route the out-of-cycle review through the same legal-review and Board-approval steps as the annual cycle.
checklist.done: every trigger event initiates an out-of-cycle review within 30 days, following the standard approval path

checklist.step: Reconcile internal controls to the approved framework
actions: Test a sample of key controls against the current approved internal-control framework.
Report any control found inconsistent with, or unaddressed by, the framework to the Audit Committee.
Recommend framework updates for the next annual cycle based on findings.
checklist.done: control testing results are reported to the Audit Committee with recommended framework updates

checklist.step: File the annual policy package and approvals in the compliance evidence repository
actions: Upload the final approved package, minutes extract, legal-review sign-off and attestation summaries into the repository.
Tag the package by fiscal year and policy name.
Confirm retrievability by policy name and approval date.
checklist.done: the annual policy package is filed, tagged and retrievable by policy name and date

checklist.step: Escalate any unresolved inconsistency between management action and approved policy
actions: Compile any attestation breach, control testing inconsistency or interim-trigger finding not yet remediated.
Present the open-items list to the Board Risk Committee with an owner and target date for each.
Confirm closure evidence before removing an item from the open list.
checklist.done: every unresolved inconsistency is presented to the Board Risk Committee with an owner and target date

testing.step: Build the population of governance policies in scope for the annual cycle
actions: Extract the full policy inventory from the board portal's policy library with last-approval dates.
Reconcile the extract to the policy list maintained by the Board Governance Lead.
Resolve any discrepancy before sampling.
testing.done: the policy population is reconciled and signed complete

testing.step: Confirm every policy was reviewed within the required 12-month cycle
actions: Compare each policy's last-approval date to the current test date.
Flag any policy older than 12 months without a documented interim-review exemption.
testing.done: every policy's review timeliness is confirmed or logged as an exception

testing.step: Re-perform the risk-appetite consistency check on the sampled business plan
actions: Independently compare the approved business plan's growth and capital assumptions to the approved risk appetite statement's limits.
Flag any inconsistency not identified and addressed in the Board package.
testing.done: risk-appetite consistency is independently confirmed, or an inconsistency is logged

testing.step: Verify legal review was completed before Board approval
actions: Pull the iManage review record for each sampled policy.
Confirm the legal-review completion date precedes the Board approval date in the minutes.
Flag any policy approved before legal review closed.
testing.done: legal-review timing is confirmed for every sampled policy, or logged as an exception

testing.step: Confirm Board approval is recorded with the correct final version
actions: Compare the version approved per the minutes to the version published in SharePoint.
Flag any mismatch, including any in-session amendment not reflected in the published version.
testing.done: the published policy version is confirmed to match the Board-approved version, or a mismatch is logged

testing.step: Test a sample of quarterly management attestations
actions: Pull a sample of business-line attestations for the test period.
Independently assess whether the underlying activity, from the risk register or business metrics, supports the attestation.
Flag any attestation that appears inconsistent with underlying activity.
testing.done: sampled attestations are independently corroborated, or inconsistencies are logged

testing.step: Confirm interim-trigger reviews were initiated within 30 days
actions: Identify any trigger event, such as an acquisition, guideline change, or risk-appetite breach, that occurred in the test period.
Confirm an out-of-cycle policy review was initiated within 30 days of the trigger.
Flag any trigger with no documented interim review.
testing.done: every trigger event has a timely interim review, or is logged as an exception

testing.step: Verify internal-control testing results were reported and addressed
actions: Pull the internal-control testing summary presented to the Audit Committee.
Confirm each material deficiency has a corresponding framework-update recommendation or remediation plan.
Flag any deficiency with no follow-up action.
testing.done: every material control deficiency has a documented follow-up, or is logged as an exception

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker entry for each testing exception (late review, inconsistency, missed legal review, unaddressed deficiency).
Assign a root cause and an owner from Board Governance Lead, General Counsel or the relevant business-line executive.
Set a remediation date and carry unresolved items into the next annual test.
testing.done: every exception has an owner, root cause and remediation date

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the governance policy review test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the 12-month review-cycle and risk-appetite-consistency standards.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence.
Have an independent reviewer who did not draft the sampled policies sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the Board Risk Committee

checklist.step: Maintain the critical third-party inventory and tiering
actions: Open the GRC platform's third-party risk register and confirm every vendor is tiered (critical, significant, standard) per the entity's third-party risk methodology.
Cross-check the critical tier against vendors supporting critical operations identified in the operational resilience program.
Flag any newly onboarded vendor missing a tiering assessment.
checklist.done: the third-party inventory is current and every critical vendor is correctly tiered

checklist.step: Confirm the information-security program document covers the required domains
actions: Review the written information-security program against Guideline B-13's control domains: identity and access management, vulnerability and patch management, secure configuration, logging and monitoring, incident response.
Confirm the program states risk-based proportionality, describing how control intensity scales with system criticality.
Update any domain section that has not been reviewed in the last 12 months.
checklist.done: the program document addresses every required B-13 control domain with a current review date

checklist.step: Review and refresh the critical-contract clause checklist
actions: Confirm the clause checklist covers service levels, security requirements, sub-contracting/fourth-party approval, business continuity, audit rights, OSFI access rights, data location/residency, and termination/exit assistance.
Update the checklist for any change in OSFI Guideline B-10 expectations.
Circulate the updated checklist to Procurement Manager and Contracts Manager.
checklist.done: an updated clause checklist is circulated to Procurement and Contracts for use in all critical-vendor negotiations

checklist.step: Screen new critical vendor contracts against the clause checklist before signature
actions: Open the draft contract in Icertis CLM and run the clause checklist against each required provision.
Flag any missing or weakened clause, such as audit rights limited to annual or OSFI-access rights absent, to the negotiation team.
Do not route the contract for signature until all required clauses are present or a documented exception is approved.
checklist.done: every new critical vendor contract passes the clause checklist or carries an approved, documented exception before signature

checklist.step: Negotiate missing or weak clauses with the vendor
actions: Present the required clause language to the vendor's contracting team, referencing the entity's standard security and TPRM addendum.
Escalate vendor pushback on OSFI access rights or audit rights to General Counsel for a risk-based decision.
Document the final negotiated clause language and any compromise reached.
checklist.done: negotiated clause language is documented, with any compromise reviewed by General Counsel

checklist.step: Obtain OSFI-access-rights clause specifically confirming regulator examination access
actions: Confirm the contract explicitly grants OSFI, and the entity's internal/external auditors, the right to examine the vendor's records and operations relevant to the outsourced activity.
Where the vendor operates offshore, confirm the clause addresses cross-border access and any local law conflict.
File the clause language extract in the vendor's GRC platform record.
checklist.done: the OSFI-access-rights clause is confirmed present and its language filed against the vendor record

checklist.step: Confirm data-location and data-residency clauses are consistent with data classification
actions: Determine the data classification of information the vendor will process, whether personal, confidential or regulated.
Confirm the contract specifies permitted data-storage and processing locations consistent with the entity's data-residency policy.
Flag any clause permitting undisclosed sub-processor locations for remediation.
checklist.done: data-location clauses match the vendor's actual data classification and processing footprint

checklist.step: Confirm sub-contracting/fourth-party provisions require notice and approval
actions: Verify the contract requires the vendor to notify and obtain approval before engaging a new material sub-contractor.
Request the vendor's current sub-contractor/fourth-party list and file it against the vendor record.
Assess whether any fourth party itself qualifies as critical and needs its own risk assessment.
checklist.done: sub-contracting notice/approval provisions are confirmed and the current fourth-party list is on file

checklist.step: Confirm business-continuity and termination/exit clauses meet the entity's requirements
actions: Verify the contract requires the vendor to maintain and test its own business continuity plan and to share test results or attestations.
Verify the termination/exit clause specifies data return or destruction, transition assistance duration, and continuity of service during transition.
Flag any contract lacking a workable exit clause for the vendor's criticality tier.
checklist.done: business-continuity and exit provisions are confirmed adequate for the vendor's tier

checklist.step: Review and remediate legacy critical contracts at renewal
actions: On each 120-day renewal alert, pull the legacy contract and run the current clause checklist against it.
Where the legacy contract predates current requirements, negotiate an amendment or addendum before renewal.
Update the Icertis CLM record with the amended clause set and new expiry date.
checklist.done: every renewing legacy critical contract is brought to current clause standard before renewal executes

checklist.step: Confirm the information-security program is approved and communicated
actions: Route the annually refreshed information-security program to the Chief Risk Officer and Board Risk Committee for approval.
Publish the approved program to IT and Security teams via the GRC platform's policy module.
Confirm acknowledgment tracking is enabled for staff required to attest to the program.
checklist.done: the program is Board-approved, published and acknowledgment tracking is active

checklist.step: Reconcile the vendor contract clause status to the GRC third-party risk register
actions: For every critical vendor, record the clause-checklist pass/fail status and any open exception in the GRC platform's vendor record.
Reconcile the count of critical vendors with complete clauses against the total critical-vendor count.
Report the reconciliation to the Chief Info Security Officer monthly.
checklist.done: the GRC register shows current clause-compliance status for every critical vendor, reconciled monthly

checklist.step: Track and close open clause exceptions
actions: Maintain an exception log for any critical contract missing a required clause, with a target remediation date.
Escalate any exception open beyond 90 days to General Counsel and the Chief Risk Officer.
Close the exception only when the amended clause is executed and filed.
checklist.done: no clause exception remains open beyond 90 days without an executive escalation on record

checklist.step: File the program and contract evidence in the compliance evidence repository
actions: Upload the approved information-security program, the clause checklist, and the critical-vendor clause-compliance report.
Tag the filing by fiscal year and 'B-10/B-13'.
Confirm retrievability by vendor name and contract expiry date.
checklist.done: program and contract evidence is filed, tagged and retrievable by vendor and expiry date

checklist.step: Brief the Board Risk Committee on third-party contract clause coverage
actions: Present the annual clause-compliance reconciliation and any aged exception to the Board Risk Committee.
Recommend remediation priority for any critical vendor still non-compliant.
Record the Committee's direction and any escalation to General Counsel in the minutes.
checklist.done: the Board Risk Committee receives the annual clause-compliance report with recorded direction on open exceptions

testing.step: Build the population of critical third-party contracts in scope
actions: Extract the critical-tier vendor list from the GRC platform's third-party risk register.
Reconcile the extract to the Icertis CLM contract repository by vendor name and contract ID.
Resolve any count mismatch before sampling.
testing.done: the critical-contract population is reconciled between the GRC register and Icertis CLM

testing.step: Select the sample of contracts for clause testing
actions: Take all contracts signed or renewed in the test period, plus a random sample of legacy contracts not yet renewed, minimum 25 contracts.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and documented

testing.step: Re-perform the clause checklist on each sampled contract
actions: Open each sampled contract in Icertis CLM and independently check for service-level, security, sub-contracting, business-continuity, audit, OSFI-access, data-location and termination/exit clauses.
Compare your finding to the recorded clause-checklist result for that contract.
Flag any discrepancy, including a clause present in name but weaker than required.
testing.done: each sampled contract has an independent clause re-check, with discrepancies flagged

testing.step: Verify OSFI-access-rights clause language is legally sufficient
actions: Read the OSFI-access-rights clause on each sampled contract for the specific language granting examination access.
Confirm the clause does not carve out data or systems relevant to the outsourced activity.
Flag any clause that is aspirational, such as 'will cooperate', rather than a binding access right.

testing.step: Confirm data-location clauses match actual vendor processing locations

checklist.step: Define the annual assessment scope
actions: Pull the current system/application inventory from the GRC platform's CMDB integration and identify systems supporting critical operations.
Confirm the scope includes internet-facing systems, core policy administration and claims platforms, and third-party connections.
Publish the scope and assessment schedule to the Security team and system owners.
checklist.done: a published scope document lists every in-scope system and the assessment schedule

checklist.step: Run the automated vulnerability scan across in-scope systems
actions: Configure the scan job in Qualys/Tenable against the in-scope asset group with authenticated credentials where available.
Execute the scan and confirm 100% of in-scope assets returned a scan result, with no scan-blocked or unreachable hosts left unresolved.
Export the findings report with CVE identifiers, CVSS scores and affected asset list.
checklist.done: a complete scan result exists for every in-scope asset with CVE/CVSS detail exported

checklist.step: Commission external penetration testing on internet-facing and critical systems
actions: Engage an independent penetration-testing provider for internet-facing applications and the core policy/claims platforms.
Provide the tester the current architecture diagram and prior findings for retest coverage.
Receive the penetration-test report with proof-of-concept detail for each finding.
checklist.done: a penetration-test report with proof-of-concept detail is received for every tested system

checklist.step: Assess third-party and cloud-configuration risk
actions: Review cloud security posture findings from the cloud provider's security center or a dedicated cloud security posture tool for misconfigurations.
Cross-reference critical third-party connections against the third-party risk register for known control gaps.
Add cloud and third-party findings to the consolidated risk assessment.
checklist.done: cloud-configuration and third-party findings are incorporated into the consolidated assessment

checklist.step: Rate and consolidate findings by severity
actions: Import scan, penetration-test and cloud-posture findings into the GRC platform's risk register.
Rate each finding critical/high/medium/low using CVSS score adjusted for exploitability and asset criticality.
De-duplicate findings reported by multiple tools against the same root cause.
checklist.done: a consolidated, de-duplicated, severity-rated finding set exists in the GRC platform

checklist.step: Assign remediation owners and SLA-driven due dates
actions: Assign each finding to the system or application owner responsible for the fix.
Set the due date per the severity SLA, critical 30 days, high 60 days, medium 90 days, from the finding's confirmed date.
Notify each owner via the GRC platform's workflow with the finding detail and remediation guidance.
checklist.done: every finding has an assigned owner and an SLA-derived due date in the GRC platform

checklist.step: Track remediation progress and escalate approaching SLA breaches
actions: Review the GRC platform's open-findings dashboard weekly for findings within 20% of their SLA deadline.
Follow up directly with the assigned owner and their manager on any finding at risk of missing SLA.
Escalate any critical finding within 5 days of SLA breach to the Chief Info Security Officer.
checklist.done: at-risk findings are followed up weekly and critical near-breaches are escalated within 5 days

checklist.step: Apply and verify patches or configuration fixes
actions: Coordinate with the system owner and Systems Administrator to deploy the vendor patch or configuration change in the maintenance window.
Confirm the change was deployed to all affected instances, not a single representative host.
Record the deployment date and change ticket reference on the finding.
checklist.done: the fix is deployed to all affected instances with a change ticket reference recorded

checklist.step: Re-scan or re-test to confirm remediation
actions: Run a targeted re-scan against the specific asset and vulnerability signature that was remediated.
For penetration-test findings, request the testing provider re-attempt the proof-of-concept exploit.
Attach the clean re-scan or retest result to the finding before closing it.
checklist.done: a clean re-scan or retest result is attached to every finding before closure

checklist.step: Document and approve any risk-acceptance in lieu of remediation
actions: Where a finding cannot be remediated within SLA, such as a legacy system or vendor dependency, review the compensating control proposed by the CISO.
Approve or reject the risk-acceptance with an expiry date requiring re-review.
Record the risk-acceptance decision and rationale in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: every SLA-missed finding has either remediation evidence or a dated, approved risk-acceptance on file

checklist.step: Report the assessment results and remediation status to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Compile the finding count by severity, SLA-compliance rate and top risk themes into the Board Risk Committee cyber-risk report.
Include the current risk-acceptance register with expiry dates.
Present the report and note any recommended additional investment.
checklist.done: the Board Risk Committee cyber-risk report is presented with severity breakdown, SLA compliance and risk-acceptance register

checklist.step: Feed assessment findings into the enterprise risk register
actions: Map material cyber findings and their remediation status into the enterprise risk register's technology/cyber risk category.
Confirm the risk rating in the enterprise register reflects the current unremediated finding severity, not a stale rating.
Link the enterprise register entry to the GRC platform finding record for traceability.
checklist.done: the enterprise risk register reflects current cyber-assessment findings with traceable links to the GRC platform

checklist.step: Trigger an out-of-cycle assessment on material change
actions: Define trigger events, such as a new critical system go-live, major architecture change, or confirmed incident, requiring an out-of-cycle assessment.
Initiate the scoped assessment within 30 days of a trigger event.
Follow the standard scan/test/rate/remediate cycle for the triggered scope.
checklist.done: every trigger event results in a scoped assessment initiated within 30 days

checklist.step: File assessment reports and remediation evidence in the compliance evidence repository
actions: Upload the vulnerability scan report, penetration-test report, GRC finding export and risk-acceptance register.
Tag the filing by assessment cycle and fiscal year.
Confirm retrievability by system name and finding severity.
checklist.done: assessment and remediation evidence is filed, tagged and retrievable by system and severity

checklist.step: Review and refresh the assessment methodology annually
actions: Compare the current methodology, including scope, tools, severity rating and SLAs, against industry practice and any OSFI B-13 guidance update.
Update the procedure and communicate changes to the Security team and system owners.
Record the methodology review date for the next annual cycle.
checklist.done: the methodology is reviewed annually with changes communicated and the review date recorded

testing.step: Build the population of cybersecurity findings from the assessment cycle
actions: Extract every finding logged in the GRC platform for the test period, with severity, owner and due date.
Reconcile the extract to the vulnerability scan and penetration-test report totals.
Resolve any discrepancy before sampling.
testing.done: the finding population is reconciled to the source reports and signed complete

testing.step: Select the sample of findings for re-verification
actions: Take all critical findings, plus a random sample of 25% of high findings, minimum 30 total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and documented, with 100% critical coverage

testing.step: Re-perform the vulnerability scan on sampled remediated findings
actions: Independently run a scan against the specific asset and CVE for each sampled remediated finding.
Compare your scan result to the closure evidence on file.
Flag any finding that reopens on independent re-scan.
testing.done: each sampled finding is independently re-scanned, with reopened findings flagged

testing.step: Verify remediation deployment reached all affected instances
actions: For each sampled finding, pull the affected-asset list from the original scan and the deployment change ticket.
Confirm the change ticket covers every affected asset, not a subset.
Flag any asset in the original finding not covered by the deployment record.
testing.done: deployment completeness is confirmed for every sampled finding, or flagged as an exception

testing.step: Recompute SLA compliance for the sampled findings
actions: For each sampled finding, recompute the SLA due date, confirmed date plus severity SLA days.
Compare to the actual closure date and flag any finding closed after its recomputed due date without a documented risk-acceptance.
testing.done: SLA compliance is independently recomputed for every sampled finding, or logged as an exception

testing.step: Verify risk-acceptance approvals for SLA-missed findings
actions: Pull the risk-acceptance record for each sampled finding that missed its SLA.
Confirm Chief Risk Officer approval, a compensating control description and an expiry date are on file.
Flag any SLA-missed finding with no risk-acceptance on file.
testing.done: every SLA-missed finding has a verified risk-acceptance, or is logged as an exception

testing.step: Trace enterprise risk register entries to GRC platform findings
actions: Pull the technology/cyber risk category entries from the enterprise risk register.
Confirm each entry's rating reflects the current unremediated finding severity in the GRC platform.
Flag any register entry with a stale rating inconsistent with open findings.
testing.done: enterprise risk register ratings are confirmed current against GRC findings, or flagged

testing.step: Confirm out-of-cycle assessments were triggered as required
actions: Identify any critical-system go-live, major architecture change or confirmed incident in the test period.
Confirm a scoped out-of-cycle assessment was initiated within 30 days.
Flag any trigger event with no corresponding assessment.
testing.done: every trigger event has a timely out-of-cycle assessment, or is logged as an exception

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker entry for each testing exception (reopened finding, incomplete deployment, SLA miss without acceptance, stale register rating).
Assign a root cause and an owner from Vulnerability Analyst, Application Security Lead or the system owner.
Set a remediation date and carry unresolved items into the next assessment cycle.
testing.done: every exception has an owner, root cause and remediation date

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the cybersecurity assessment test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the SLA-compliance and risk-acceptance-governance standards.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence.
Have an independent reviewer who did not perform the sampled remediations sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the Board Risk Committee

checklist.step: Confirm MFA is enforced on all in-scope access paths

checklist.step: Verify encryption-at-rest is applied to sensitive data stores

checklist.step: Verify encryption-in-transit on external and internal sensitive data flows

checklist.done: the quarterly campaign completes with all access attested, revoked or escalated within the campaign window

checklist.step: Run the monthly privileged-access recertification

Confirm every privileged account is still required and tied to an active employee or service need.
Revoke any privileged access not recertified within the monthly window.
checklist.done: every privileged account is recertified monthly, with unrecertified access revoked

checklist.step: De-provision access on termination and role change within SLA

Confirm access is revoked within 24 hours of a termination and adjusted within 5 business days of a role change.
Log any de-provisioning missed against SLA as an exception.
checklist.done: terminated and transferred users have their access revoked or adjusted within the defined SLA, with any miss logged

checklist.step: Apply security patches within the defined SLA

Deploy critical patches within 30 days, high within 60 days, following the change-management process for production systems.
Confirm patch deployment via a targeted re-scan before marking the patch item closed.
checklist.done: patches are deployed within their SLA and confirmed via re-scan before closure

checklist.step: Maintain secure configuration baselines

Flag and remediate any configuration drift, such as an open management port or a disabled logging agent.
Update the baseline document annually or on any major platform version change.
checklist.done: configuration drift is identified and remediated against a current baseline

checklist.step: Operate centralized security logging and monitoring

checklist.done: all in-scope systems are confirmed logging to the SIEM, with source gaps ticketed and correlation rules reviewed quarterly

checklist.step: Triage and respond to SOC alerts

Escalate confirmed true-positive alerts to the Incident Response Lead per the escalation procedure.

checklist.done: alerts are triaged within target response time with disposition and response time logged

checklist.step: Report control operating metrics to the Chief Info Security Officer monthly

Highlight any metric trending outside the acceptable range.
Present the report to the Chief Info Security Officer for action prioritization.
checklist.done: a monthly control metrics report is compiled and presented with any adverse trend highlighted

checklist.step: Reconcile control evidence into the GRC platform's control library

Set each control's operating-effectiveness status based on the current evidence.
Flag any control lacking current-period evidence.
checklist.done: every layered control has current evidence attached in the GRC platform with an operating-effectiveness status

checklist.step: File control operating evidence in the compliance evidence repository

Tag the filing by quarter and control domain.
Confirm retrievability by control domain and reporting period.
checklist.done: control operating evidence is filed, tagged and retrievable by control domain and period

checklist.step: Escalate persistent control gaps to the Board Risk Committee

Present the gap, root cause and remediation plan to the Board Risk Committee.
Record the Committee's direction and any resourcing approval in the minutes.

Reconcile the extract to the HRIS active-employee list and the system inventory maintained by IT.
Resolve any discrepancy before sampling.
testing.done: the account and system population is reconciled and signed complete

Flag any sampled account without active MFA enrollment.

Flag any store found unencrypted or using a deprecated key-management scheme.
testing.done: encryption is independently confirmed for every sampled store, or flagged

testing.step: Verify privileged accounts are vaulted and time-bound

Confirm each is onboarded to CyberArk's vault and configured for time-bound checkout, not a static credential.
Flag any privileged account found outside the vault.
testing.done: privileged-account vaulting is confirmed for every sampled account, or flagged

Flag any user with no completed recertification action.

Flag any de-provisioning action outside the defined SLA.
testing.done: de-provisioning timeliness is confirmed for every sampled user, or flagged as an exception

Flag any patch deployed after its recomputed SLA due date.
testing.done: patch SLA compliance is independently recomputed for every sampled item, or flagged

Flag any critical system with a stale or missing log feed.
testing.done: SIEM log-source coverage is confirmed for every sampled critical system, or flagged

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date

Set a remediation date and carry unresolved items into the next quarterly test.
testing.done: every exception has an owner, root cause and remediation date
