checklist.step: Contain and investigate the incident
actions: Isolate affected systems per the plan's containment playbook for the incident type, such as ransomware, data exfiltration, DDoS, or third-party compromise.
Preserve forensic evidence, including logs, memory captures and disk images, before remediation actions overwrite it.
Update the ITSM ticket with containment actions taken and their timestamps.
checklist.done: containment actions are documented with timestamps and forensic evidence is preserved before remediation

checklist.step: Escalate to the Chief Info Security Officer and Chief Risk Officer
actions: Notify the Chief Info Security Officer immediately on any incident classified medium severity or above.
Brief the Chief Risk Officer on any incident meeting the OSFI-reportability trigger, including known impact to critical operations.
Confirm the CEO and Board Risk Committee chair are briefed for any incident assessed as materially impacting the entity.
checklist.done: escalation to CISO, CRO and, where material, CEO/Board chair is confirmed with timestamps for reportable incidents

checklist.step: Prepare and submit the OSFI technology and cyber incident notification
actions: Complete the OSFI Technology and Cyber Security Incident Reporting form with incident description, systems/operations affected, current status and containment actions.
Submit the notification to OSFI as promptly as possible and no later than 24 hours after the incident is assessed as reportable.
Record the submission time and any OSFI acknowledgment received.
checklist.done: the OSFI notification is submitted within 24 hours of reportability determination, with submission time and acknowledgment on record

checklist.step: Provide OSFI-required follow-up updates until incident closure
actions: Provide periodic status updates to OSFI per the advisory's expectations until the incident is contained and assessed.
Submit a final incident report summarizing root cause, impact, and remediation once resolved.
File all OSFI correspondence in the incident record.
checklist.done: periodic updates and a final report are provided to OSFI and filed against the incident record

checklist.step: Recover affected systems and confirm recovery objectives are met
actions: Execute the recovery runbook for the affected system, restoring from a verified clean backup or rebuild.
Measure actual recovery time against the system's defined Recovery Time Objective and Recovery Point Objective.
Record any RTO/RPO breach and its business impact in the incident ticket.
checklist.done: systems are recovered with actual RTO/RPO measured against target and any breach documented

checklist.step: Conduct the post-incident root-cause review
actions: Hold a root-cause review with responders, system owners and the Chief Info Security Officer within 10 business days of incident closure.
Document the root cause, contributing factors, and what worked or failed in the response.
Assign remediation actions with owners and target dates.
checklist.done: a root-cause review is held within 10 business days with documented findings and assigned remediation actions

checklist.step: Plan and schedule the annual incident response plan test
actions: Select the test scenario, tabletop or live/functional exercise, covering a critical-operation-impacting cyber scenario, rotating scenario type year over year.
Schedule the test with all required responders, including the Chief Risk Officer and, for major scenarios, a Board Risk Committee observer.
Confirm the test includes exercising the OSFI notification workflow, not only technical containment.
checklist.done: an annual test is scheduled with a defined scenario that exercises both containment and the OSFI notification workflow

checklist.step: Execute the incident response plan test
actions: Facilitate the test per the scenario script, injecting realistic decision points and timing pressure.
Time each key milestone: detection-to-classification, classification-to-escalation, and classification-to-notification-readiness.
Capture participant decisions and any deviation from the documented plan.
checklist.done: the test is executed with timed milestones and captured decisions against the documented plan

checklist.step: Produce the test after-action report
actions: Compare timed milestones against the plan's target response times, including the 24-hour OSFI notification readiness target.
Identify plan gaps, unclear ownership, or tooling failures observed during the test.
Assign remediation owners and target dates for each identified gap.
checklist.done: an after-action report with milestone comparison and assigned remediation actions is produced

checklist.step: Update the plan based on test findings and real-incident lessons
actions: Revise the plan's escalation matrix, playbooks or contact lists per the after-action report's findings.
Route the revised plan to the Chief Info Security Officer and Chief Risk Officer for approval.
Version and date the approved plan and communicate the change to responders.
checklist.done: the plan is revised, approved and versioned, with the change communicated to responders

checklist.step: File test and incident evidence in the compliance evidence repository
actions: Upload the after-action report, incident tickets, OSFI notification submissions and acknowledgments, and the updated plan.
Tag the filing by incident/test date and 'B-13 incident management'.
Confirm retrievability by incident ID and date.
checklist.done: test and incident evidence is filed, tagged and retrievable by incident ID and date

checklist.step: Report incident management performance to the Board Risk Committee annually
actions: Compile the year's incident count by severity, OSFI notification timeliness, and the annual test outcome.
Present the summary and any material recommendation to the Board Risk Committee.
Record the Committee's direction, including any resourcing or plan-change approval, in the minutes.
checklist.done: an annual incident management performance summary is presented with recorded Board Risk Committee direction

testing.step: Build the population of incidents and the annual test event
actions: Extract every incident ticket classified medium severity or above from the ITSM platform for the test period, plus the annual plan-test record.
Reconcile the extract to the SOC's alert-to-incident escalation log.
Resolve any discrepancy before sampling.
testing.done: the incident population is reconciled to the SOC escalation log and signed complete

testing.step: Select the sample of incidents and confirm the annual test occurred
actions: Take all incidents assessed as potentially OSFI-reportable, plus a random sample of five other medium+ incidents.
Confirm the annual incident response plan test occurred within the required 12-month window.
Record the sample and confirmation in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn with 100% coverage of reportable incidents, and the annual test's occurrence is confirmed

testing.step: Recompute the 24-hour OSFI notification clock for each sampled reportable incident
actions: Independently determine the time the incident met the reportability trigger from the ITSM ticket history.
Compute 24 hours from that time and compare to the actual OSFI notification submission timestamp.
Flag any notification submitted after the recomputed 24-hour deadline.
testing.done: the 24-hour clock is independently recomputed for every sampled reportable incident, with any breach flagged

testing.step: Verify escalation timestamps against the plan's target response times
actions: Pull the detection, classification, and escalation timestamps from the ITSM ticket for each sampled incident.
Compare elapsed time between stages to the plan's documented target response times.
Flag any stage that exceeded its target without a documented justification.
testing.done: escalation timing is independently verified against plan targets for every sampled incident, or flagged

testing.step: Confirm forensic evidence preservation on sampled incidents
actions: Check the incident record for evidence of log/forensic preservation actions taken before remediation.
Confirm chain-of-custody documentation exists for any evidence later used in root-cause analysis or a regulatory response.
Flag any incident where remediation appears to have occurred before evidence preservation.
testing.done: evidence preservation is confirmed for every sampled incident, or flagged as an exception

testing.step: Verify recovery objectives were measured and any breach documented
actions: Pull the RTO/RPO target for each affected system from the business continuity plan.
Compare to the actual recovery time recorded on the sampled incident ticket.
Flag any RTO/RPO breach not documented with business-impact assessment.
testing.done: recovery-objective measurement is confirmed for every sampled incident, or flagged

testing.step: Verify the root-cause review occurred within 10 business days
actions: Confirm a documented root-cause review exists for each sampled incident, with the review date compared to the incident closure date.
Confirm remediation actions from the review have assigned owners and target dates.
Flag any incident with no root-cause review or an overdue review.
testing.done: root-cause reviews are confirmed timely for every sampled incident, or flagged as an exception

testing.step: Re-perform milestone timing analysis on the annual test
actions: Pull the after-action report's timed milestones for the annual plan test.
Independently verify the reported timings against the raw test log or facilitator notes.
Confirm the test exercised the OSFI notification-readiness workflow, not only technical containment.
testing.done: test timing and notification-workflow coverage are independently verified against the raw test record

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker entry for each testing exception (late notification, missed target timing, evidence-preservation gap, missing root-cause review).
Assign a root cause and an owner from Incident Response Lead, SOC Lead or Chief Info Security Officer.
Set a remediation date and carry unresolved items, including any missed 24-hour notification, into a mandatory self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
testing.done: every exception has an owner, root cause and remediation date, with missed notifications escalated for self-report assessment

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the incident response test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance standard for missed 24-hour OSFI notifications.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence.
Have an independent reviewer who did not respond to the sampled incidents sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any open breach to the Board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the Board Risk Committee
